review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. NOAA/USGS early-life thermal studies and NOAA habitat synthesis added; SST and depth claims are partly supported with explicit life-stage caveats.

profile.size: Min limit 22 inches TL / Bag limit 3-5 per harvester / day

profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for california halibut.
factors.value_notes: NOAA's California halibut SST assessment uses 12-20 °C as an egg-suitability threshold based on laboratory egg development; USGS experiments found eggs hatched at 12, 16 and 20 °C but not at 8 or 24 °C. Juvenile studies report preferred temperatures varying with acclimation (15.1-24.7 °C; final preferendum 18.4 °C). This supports thermal relevance, but egg and juvenile responses differ and do not establish a universal adult SST catch curve. The configured 12-21 °C / 14-19 °C bands remain provisional for mixed life stages.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for california halibut.
factors.value_notes: NOAA's 2025 species synthesis reports mature California halibut in nearshore coastal waters to about 100 m, with most mature fish shallower than 30 m; juveniles rely on estuaries and embayments. This supports shallow demersal habitat but the configured 2-60 m band and 4-55 m ideal extend well beyond the depth range used by most mature fish and do not represent nursery habitat separately.
